article_content: In a significant move for marine conservation, President Bush announced the creation of nine new sanctuaries in the central Pacific. These areas, spanning 195,280 square miles, are now the world's largest marine conservation zones. The sanctuaries will not only serve as havens for marine life but also as crucial research sites for scientists. Using the 1906 Antiquities Act, a law first utilized by President Theodore Roosevelt, Bush designated these areas as national monuments. The Marine Conservation Biology Institute and the Environmental Defense Fund collaborated to identify eight of these sites, which include Rose Atoll, Wake Island, Johnston Island, Palmyra Island, Kingman Reef, Baker Island, Howland Island, and Jarvis Island. The ninth site, identified by the Pew Environmental Fund, encompasses the waters around the Northern Marianas and the Mariana Trench, the deepest part of the world's oceans. The new designations extend protection to a 50 nautical mile radius around the islands, banning commercial fishing within this zone. While other activities like research and recreational fishing will be permitted, they will require special permits. Additionally, President Bush revealed plans to nominate George Washington's historic home, Mount Vernon, and the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands Marine National Monument as UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Two years prior, Bush had already designated 138,000 square miles in Hawaii as a protected marine area, making it the largest fully protected marine zone globally at the time.

article_content: Washington (CNN) -- A Secret Service agent suspected of having a romantic relationship with a Mexican woman has died of an apparent suicide, a law enforcement official told CNN on Thursday. The source said Rafael Prieto, 48, was assigned to President Obama's protective detail. The Secret Service confirmed on Thursday that Prieto's death last Saturday is currently being investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department in Washington, along with the medical examiner's office. No official determination of death has been made. Prieto's access to Secret Service facilities had been suspended while authorities were looking into his apparently unreported and long-term relationship with a foreign national, the law enforcement official said. 'There is nothing to indicate that any classified or sensitive information was compromised as a result of this relationship,' according to the source. The official said Prieto was involved in an 'administrative process' about his connection with the woman but that he was not under investigation by the Secret Service's Office of Professional Responsibility. Prieto could have been in violation of Secret Service protocols if he had not informed superiors about a personal relationship with a foreign national. Such relationships came under a spotlight after agents sent to Cartagena, Colombia, in advance of President Obama's trip earlier this year spent time partying with prostitutes. 'Rafael Prieto had a distinguished 20-year career with the Secret Service that was marked by accomplishment, dedication, and friendships,' said Secret Service spokesman Edwin Donovan. 'The Secret Service is mourning the loss of a valued colleague.'

article_content: Approximately one-fifth of young married individuals in Britain confess to taking off their wedding rings before social outings or following arguments with their partners, according to recent research findings. Although both genders are now more inclined to wear wedding rings compared to past generations, those under 40 are also more prone to removing them. The primary reasons cited for this behavior include seeking more attention from the opposite sex, discomfort, and making a statement during marital disagreements. One in eight participants believed they would be perceived as 'boring' if others knew they were married, while over a third attributed their actions to work-related reasons, claiming better business opportunities without a ring. Men tend to remove their rings before socializing, whereas women do so more frequently after fights. However, over 80% of men caught by their wives could not justify their actions convincingly. The study, involving 2,000 married couples, was conducted by Slater & Gordon as part of their yearly marriage analysis. Kaleel Anwar, a family lawyer at Slater & Gordon, noted that many clients experience frustration due to their partners' reluctance to wear rings, often leading to trust issues. He observed that as ring-wearing has become more common, its removal can be seen as a sign of potential infidelity. Despite these concerns, younger individuals place greater importance on wearing wedding bands and are more likely to feel hurt if their partner refuses to wear one. Younger men view the ring as a crucial part of their marital commitment, with 27% more likely to wear one compared to those over 40. Women also emphasize the importance of their partners wearing rings, with 28% finding it disrespectful if their partner removes it. Anwar cautioned against relying too heavily on material symbols like rings, stating that they do not guarantee relationship stability. Interestingly, one in ten participants felt that wearing a ring was seen as a 'challenge' by the opposite sex, with men reporting increased attention and women experiencing the opposite effect. Nearly two-thirds of respondents believed that others respect the commitment symbolized by the ring.

article_content: By Harriet Arkell and Richard Shears  A young couple, feared to have fallen to their deaths from a luxury cruise liner off the coast of Australia, reportedly had a heated argument on the night of the incident. CCTV footage shows Paul Rossington, 30, and Kristen Schroder, 27, arguing in the ship's casino on Wednesday, according to the Sydney Herald. The couple subsequently missed a planned dinner with Ms. Schroder's family, who were also traveling on the Carnival Spirit liner.  A source told the Sydney Herald that the couple frequently had short but intense arguments. 'It was a common occurrence between them,' the source said.  Senior police sources revealed that CCTV footage captures Ms. Schroder falling from the ship first, followed by her paramedic boyfriend. Further footage shows Ms. Schroder hitting a lifeboat before her body hit the water. The couple had been traveling with a group of friends and family on the Carnival Spirit liner.  The extensive sea and air search for the pair was called off yesterday. Authorities are considering the theory that Ms. Schroder fell first and her boyfriend then jumped in to try to save her. 'Paul was trying to save her,' a source told the Australian Associated Press.  Security footage on the boat shows the pair falling overboard from the mid-deck as the ship traveled down the New South Wales' mid-north coast just before 9 pm local time on Wednesday. Ms. Schroder wrote on her Twitter feed about her excitement for the holiday days before they boarded the cruise liner.  Initially, police could not determine who fell into the sea first, but after enhancing the footage, they confirmed that it was Ms. Schroder who plunged first from the 65ft-high deck, followed about 20 seconds later by her boyfriend. They were reported missing 12 hours later after the boat docked at Sydney's Circular Quay at the end of its 10-day cruise. Staff noticed the couple had not collected their luggage when the rest of the 2,680 passengers disembarked.  Survival expert Dr. Paul Luckin said if the couple, from Barraba, near Tamworth in NSW, had survived the impact of hitting the water, fatigue would be their biggest problem. Dr. Luckin, who advises the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA), said he would not expect anyone to last more than three days after falling from a ship. He told the Sydney Herald: 'If you're stuck in the water and constantly being hit in the face by water, that is tremendously fatiguing... It will certainly be under three days that you would expect somebody to survive without water in those conditions.'  The couple was on holiday with a group of seven relatives and friends when they went missing on Wednesday night. Their cabin on the ship remains sealed off while forensic officers inspect it, although the ship set sail from Sydney on its next cruise at 6:30 pm last night.  NSW police marine area commander Mark Hutchings said the couple's fall was not believed to be suspicious, and officers were inspecting the ship's CCTV footage. He said: 'It’s very unclear, but it does depict one person going over and then a short time later another person going over.' The ship was about 120 km (75 miles) off the coastal town of Forster when the couple plunged into the sea.  A statement released by Carnival Cruise Lines said: 'As part of our standard protocol, a full ship search was conducted as well as an examination of closed-circuit video. There is an indication from the shipboard video of what transpired. There is no evidence of foul play. However, out of respect for the families, we are not going to publicly disclose the details of what occurred.' The firm's spokesman said the rails on the cabin balconies are higher than the required standard.  Carnival Cruise Lines, operated by Miami-based Carnival Corp, has faced a series of problems and onboard crimes including power outages, rape, sickness, and theft. Several lawsuits have been launched against Carnival, but whether complainants will have any success is doubtful as the cruise company has a legal structure that shields it from big-money lawsuits. Many passengers unknowingly sign Carnival's contracts prohibiting them from class action lawsuits, while the small print also bans them from suing on the grounds of emotional distress.  Passengers for the next Carnival Spirit cruise lined up ready to board it yesterday as the search of the ship continued. The Carnival Spirit liner set sail again last night on another cruise, but the couple's cabin remained sealed off.
translated_content: Av Harriet Arkell och Richard Shears  Ett ungt par, som fruktas ha störtat till sin död från en lyxkryssning utanför Australiens kust, ska ha haft ett hetsigt gräl på kvällen för incidenten. Övervakningsfilm visar Paul Rossington, 30, och Kristen Schroder, 27, gräla i fartygets kasino på onsdagen enligt Sydney Herald. Paret missade sedan en planerad middag med Ms. Schroders familj, som också reste på Carnival Spirit-fartyget.  En källa berättade för Sydney Herald att paret ofta hade korta men intensiva gräl. 'Det var en vanlig företeelse mellan dem,' sa källan.  Poliskällor avslöjade att övervakningsfilm visar Ms. Schroder falla från fartyget först, följt av hennes sjuksköterskepojkvän. Ytterligare film visar Ms. Schroder träffa en livbåt innan hennes kropp träffade vattnet. Paret hade rest med en grupp vänner och familj på Carnival Spirit-fartyget.  Den omfattande sökningen efter paret i havet och luften avbröts igår. Myndigheterna överväger teorin att Ms. Schroder föll först och att hennes pojkvän sedan hoppade in för att försöka rädda henne. 'Paul försökte rädda henne,' sa en källa till Australian Associated Press.  Säkerhetsfilm på båten visar paret falla överbord från mellan-däcket när fartyget färdades längs New South Wales mid-north coast klockan nio på kvällen på onsdagen. Ms. Schroder skrev på sin Twitter-flöde om sin spänning inför semestern dagar innan de gick ombord på kryssningsfartyget.  Polisen kunde initialt inte avgöra vem som föll i havet först, men efter att ha förbättrat filmen kunde de bekräfta att det var Ms. Schroder som föll först från den 65 fot höga däcket, följt cirka 20 sekunder senare av hennes pojkvän. De rapporterades saknade 12 timmar senare efter att båten anlöpte Sydney's Circular Quay i slutet av sin 10-dagars kryssning. Personalen märkte att paret inte hade hämtat sitt bagage när resten av de 2,680 passagerarna gick i land.  Överlevnadsexperten Dr. Paul Luckin sa att om paret, från Barraba, nära Tamworth i NSW, hade överlevt påverkan av att träffa vattnet, skulle trötthet bli deras största problem. Dr. Luckin, som rådgiver Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA), sa att han inte förväntar sig att någon skulle överleva mer än tre dagar efter att ha fallit från ett fartyg. Han sa till Sydney Herald: 'Om du fastnar i vattnet och ständigt blir träffad i ansiktet av vatten, är det mycket utmattande... Det kommer säkert att vara mindre än tre dagar som man skulle förvänta sig att någon skulle överleva utan vatten under dessa förhållanden.'  Paret var på semester med en grupp av sju släktingar och vänner när de försvann på onsdagskvällen. Deras hytt på fartyget förblir avstängd medan rättsmedicinska tjänstemän undersöker den, även om fartyget avgick från Sydney på sin nästa kryssning klockan 18.30 igår kväll.  NSW polischef Mark Hutchings sa att paret's fall inte ansågs vara misstänkt, och tjänstemän undersökte fartygets övervakningsfilm. Han sa: 'Det är mycket oklart, men det visar en person gå över och sedan en kort stund senare en annan person gå över.' Fartyget var cirka 120 km (75 miles) utanför kuststaden Forster när paret störtade i havet.  Ett uttalande från Carnival Cruise Lines sa: 'Som en del av vår standardprotokoll genomfördes en full sökning av fartyget samt en granskning av sluten kretsvideo. Det finns en indikation från fartygets video på vad som hände. Det finns inga bevis för olagligt spel. Av respekt för familjerna kommer vi dock inte att offentliggöra detaljerna om vad som inträffade.' Företagets talesman sa att räckena på hyttbalongerna är högre än det krävda standard.  Carnival Cruise Lines, som drivs av Miami-baserade Carnival Corp, har ställts inför en serie problem och brott ombord, inklusive strömavbrott, våldtäkt, sjukdom och stöld. Flera stämningar har väckts mot Carnival, men om klaganden kommer att ha någon framgång är tvivelaktigt eftersom kryssningsbolaget har en juridisk struktur som skyddar det från stämningar med stora pengar. Många passagerare ovetande skriver under på Carnivals kontrakt som förbjuder dem från samlingsstämningar, medan småstilen också förbjuder dem att stämma på grund av psykisk påfrestning.  Passagerare för nästa Carnival Spirit-kryssning ställde upp sig redo att gå ombord igår medan sökningen efter fartyget fortsatte. Carnival Spirit-fartyget avgick igår kväll på en annan kryssning, men paret's hytt förblev avstängd.

article_content: It's remarkable how quickly the words of Marina Keegan, a 22-year-old woman whose life was suddenly cut short, have spread across the internet and touched people worldwide. Keegan, an aspiring writer, had already been published by the New York Times and secured a job at the New Yorker. Additionally, as a playwright, she had a musical set to premiere at the New York International Fringe Festival in August. Just days after penning an inspiring essay for the Yale Daily News to motivate her graduating class, Keegan tragically died in a car accident. Her essay, which emphasized the vast potential and endless possibilities ahead for her peers, has gained profound significance following her death. In her writing, Keegan urged her fellow graduates not to lose their sense of possibility, reminding them that 'we have so much time' and can always start anew. The loss of Keegan is devastating, particularly because she embodied the rare spirit of someone who pursues and achieves their dreams. Having experienced the 'sense of possibility' Keegan described during my own time at Yale, I've seen firsthand what sets dream-chasers apart from those who give up. Friends from Yale have expressed feeling 'betrayed' by peers who abandoned their ambitious plans post-graduation, opting instead for conventional paths focused on wealth and status. These unfulfilled dreams were more than just plans; they were a pact to use our education and opportunities to make the world a better place. Keegan's final words to her class, 'Let's make something happen to this world,' echo this sentiment. The world needs more visionaries who, like Keegan, would have relentlessly pursued their dreams. Life can be exhausting and distracting, but the reward of achieving one's aspirations is unparalleled. Keegan's writing, filled with youthful optimism, serves as a poignant counterpoint to the reflections of Yale's class of 1942, who often regretted risks not taken and lives passively lived. Her words remind us to value our dreams and the time we spend with loved ones, underscoring that nothing should stop us from living with passion and conviction. Tragically, Keegan's death also highlights the ongoing issue of car crash fatalities, a pain known by too many families. Above all, Keegan cherished her family and friends, a wisdom beyond her years that inspires us to live better, more meaningful lives.
translated_content: Det är anmärkningsvärt hur snabbt Marina Keegans ord, en 22-årig kvinna vars liv plötsligt avbröts, har spridits över internet och rört människor världen över. Keegan, en lovande författare, hade redan publicerats av New York Times och säkrat ett jobb på The New Yorker. Dessutom, som dramatiker, hade hon en musikal inställd att ha premiär på New York International Fringe Festival i augusti. Endast dagar efter att ha skrivit en inspirerande artikel för Yale Daily News för att motivera sin examensklass, dog Keegan tragiskt i en bilolycka. Hennes artikel, som betonade den stora potentialen och de oändliga möjligheterna som låg framför hennes kamrater, har fått en djup betydelse efter hennes död. I sitt skrivande uppmanade Keegan sina kamrater att inte förlora sin känsla av möjlighet och påminde dem om att 'vi har så mycket tid' och alltid kan börja om. Förlusten av Keegan är förkrossande, särskilt eftersom hon förkroppsligade den sällsynta andan hos någon som förföljer och uppnår sina drömmar. Efter att ha upplevt den 'känsla av möjlighet' som Keegan beskrev under min tid på Yale, har jag sett med egna ögon vad som skiljer drömjägare från dem som ger upp. Vänner från Yale har uttryckt en känsla av 'förräderi' av kamrater som övergav sina ambitiösa planer efter examen, och istället valde konventionella vägar fokuserade på rikedom och status. Dessa ofullbordade drömmar var mer än bara planer; de var en pakt att använda vår utbildning och möjligheter för att göra världen till ett bättre ställe. Keegans sista ord till sin klass, 'Låt oss göra något till den här världen', speglar denna känsla. Världen behöver fler visionärer som, liksom Keegan, skulle ha förföljt sina drömmar outtröttligt. Livet kan vara utmattande och avledande, men belöningen för att uppnå sina strävanden är oöverträffad. Keegans skrivande, fyllt av ungdomlig optimism, tjänar som en punkt mot reflektionerna från Yales klass av 1942, som ofta ångrade risker som inte tagits och liv som levts passivt. Hennes ord påminner oss om att värdera våra drömmar och den tid vi tillbringar med våra närmasta, och understryker att ingenting ska hindra oss från att leva med passion och övertygelse. Tragiskt nog påminner Keegans död oss också om det pågående problemet med dödsolyckor i biltrafiken, en smärta som är känd av för många familjer. Främst av allt uppskattade Keegan sin familj och vänner, en visdom bortom hennes år som inspirerar oss att leva bättre, mer meningsfulla liv.

Throughout history, art has been a vital element of Palestinian resistance and a tool to reaffirm political existence. As the conflict continues, artists worldwide have been using their work to show support and solidarity with the Palestinian people. From graffiti to skateboarding, Palestinian artists have found unique ways to connect, share experiences, and ensure that their culture and identity are not erased. Presenter: Anelise Borges.
